am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI
justification: I mapped Web UI to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI because it is the operator-facing interface used to view printer status, control jobs, and interact with the machine during build execution.
purpose: Present a realistic browser-accessible printer-management surface for reconnaissance and interaction.
output_state_change: HTTP/HTTPS pages and management views that expose believable printer identity, status, and controls.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network
justification: I mapped REST API to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network because the API exposes printer/job management functions and also carries file-transfer operations into the printer workflow.
purpose: Provide programmatic printer-management endpoints for status queries, files, jobs, and commands.
output_state_change: Structured JSON request/response behavior tied to the shared simulated printer state.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped WebSocket to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it streams live machine, job, and sensor state while also carrying real-time operational events over the network.
purpose: Stream live printer, job, and sensor state so exposed services do not appear static.
output_state_change: Continuous real-time telemetry reflecting changes in the simulator and active interactions.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Telnet to Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because Telnet provides the network transport while the session directly exchanges firmware-style G-code commands and responses.
purpose: Expose a direct firmware-style console independent of the web-management layer.
output_state_change: Interactive low-level command/response sessions using the simulated firmware state.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network
justification: I mapped Other Services to Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network because optional services such as SSH or MQTT represent additional operational-network entry points around the printer environment.
purpose: Allow the exposed network personality to include additional believable printer-related services when configured.
output_state_change: Profile-controlled optional service exposure without changing the underlying simulated printer state.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Firmware Identity to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because version, capability, and firmware-identification responses are generated by the emulated firmware layer.
purpose: Return believable firmware version, capability, and identity information during reconnaissance.
output_state_change: Profile-consistent firmware identity and capability responses such as Marlin-style identification output.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Printer Profile to Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because the profile defines machine-specific physical limits and identity while also controlling firmware-facing capabilities and responses.
purpose: Let one deployment present different printer models, limits, capabilities, and firmware-facing characteristics.
output_state_change: Model-specific identity, dimensions, limits, and selected behavior exposed consistently across services.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped Access Logging to Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it records source addresses, requests, endpoints, and service-access events generated through network interactions.
purpose: Capture reconnaissance and service-access activity from the first interaction.
output_state_change: Timestamped access events including source, service, endpoint/action, and basic client metadata.

am_process_mapping: Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization; Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels
justification: I mapped Authentication to Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization and Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels because credentials and API keys are validated by the authentication layer and are used to establish authorized identity-based access.

output_state_change: Authentication/session state plus structured success/failure events for later analysis.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Command Handler to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it routes high-level management actions as well as low-level firmware commands to the appropriate execution path.
purpose: Normalize incoming management actions and commands before they update firmware or printer state.
output_state_change: Validated actions routed to file, job, state, or firmware handlers with source/channel context.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped State Management to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it maintains the job, device, and session state that must remain consistent across management controls and firmware behavior.
purpose: Keep web, API, Telnet, firmware, and telemetry views synchronized around one coherent runtime state.
output_state_change: Consistent session, job, device, and interaction state available to all active interfaces.

am_process_mapping: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network
justification: I mapped File Management to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network because it stores G-code job files locally and manages their upload, selection, and transfer into the printer workflow.

output_state_change: Updated virtual file inventory plus persistent attacker-supplied files and associated metadata.

am_process_mapping: Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization; Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels
justification: I mapped Session Control to Stage 1 > Software > Authentication / authorization and Stage 1 > Network > Identity & access channels because authenticated sessions preserve the identity and access context established after successful login.

output_state_change: Session creation, expiry, logout, and authenticated-access state shared by relevant host services.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network; Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links
justification: I mapped Network Simulation to Stage 3 > Network > OT / industrial network and Stage 3 > Network > Ethernet / Wi-Fi / USB links because it models communication effects such as latency, jitter, packet loss, and availability on the printer's operational network connections.
purpose: Model imperfect printer-network conditions instead of deterministic zero-delay communication.
output_state_change: Configurable delay, loss, and availability decisions that can be applied to host-facing traffic.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels

purpose: Preserve host-domain actions with enough context for later cross-stage reconstruction.
output_state_change: Correlated access events with session/source/channel context ready for Stage 5 storage and analysis.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped G-code Parser to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it interprets and validates G-code commands before they are executed by the simulated firmware.
purpose: Parse incoming G-code/firmware commands, validate syntax/parameters, and identify the requested operation.
output_state_change: Normalized validated command objects or believable firmware-style errors for invalid input.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer
justification: I mapped Printer State to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control and Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer because the state machine tracks firmware-controlled values that represent the current physical condition of the emulated printer.
purpose: Track motion, thermal, extrusion, power, job, and fault state as commands and simulated physics evolve.
output_state_change: One coherent printer-state representation used by firmware responses, telemetry, and downstream physical models.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC)
justification: I mapped Command Executor to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control and Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC) because it executes validated firmware commands and applies the resulting controller-level state changes.
purpose: Execute validated commands against the simulated printer and generate believable protocol-specific responses.
output_state_change: State changes and Marlin/Klipper-style acknowledgements, status replies, or fault responses.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics
justification: I mapped Sensor Emulation to Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors and Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics because it generates virtual sensor readings that are consumed as runtime monitoring data.
purpose: Expose believable thermistor, endstop, filament, and other sensor observations instead of perfect internal model values.
output_state_change: Sensor readings and sensor/fault events consumed by firmware, telemetry, and analyst logging.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Firmware Adapter to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it translates Marlin and Klipper command dialects into a common internal firmware-control interface.
purpose: Support multiple firmware dialects while keeping one coherent underlying printer state.
output_state_change: Marlin- and Klipper-style commands translated into shared simulator actions and protocol-specific responses.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Job Control to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because start, pause, resume, and cancel operations are initiated through build controls and must also update firmware job state.
purpose: Support print start, pause, resume, cancel, and job-state transitions through management and firmware paths.
output_state_change: Consistent print-job lifecycle state propagated to commands, telemetry, and the physical simulator.

am_process_mapping: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Virtual SD to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it stores printer-local G-code files and exposes them through firmware commands for selection and execution.
purpose: Expose realistic printer-local file listing, selection, persistence, and print-file behavior.
output_state_change: Persistent G-code inventory that firmware commands and management APIs can reference consistently.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics
justification: I mapped Risk Classifier to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics because it evaluates command context and assigns runtime risk labels that support ongoing analysis and alert generation.
purpose: Assign consistent risk context to relevant firmware actions for alerting and analysis.
output_state_change: Command risk labels with normalized intent, source dialect, and context passed to Stage 5 evidence handling.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC)
justification: I mapped Motion Model to Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer, Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control, and Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC) because it simulates physical X/Y/Z movement produced by firmware motion commands and controller-driven stepper behavior.
purpose: Simulate X/Y/Z position changes and stepper-driven movement caused by firmware and G-code commands.
output_state_change: Axis positions, movement status, motion_active state, and believable motion telemetry.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Extrusion Model to Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it simulates physical material flow that is commanded through extrusion-related G-code and firmware logic.
purpose: Simulate filament/material flow so extrusion behavior is consistent with movement, temperature, and print activity.
output_state_change: Extrusion amount/rate and material-flow state that change consistently with commands and simulated printing.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer; Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Thermal Model to Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer, Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors, and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it models hotend/bed heating physics, produces temperature readings, and responds to firmware temperature setpoints.
purpose: Simulate hotend and bed heating/cooling, target temperatures, and thermal limits.
output_state_change: Current/target temperatures, heating/cooling behavior, and believable thermal fault state for out-of-range setpoints.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer; Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC); Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Power & Failure Model to Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer, Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC), and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because power, shutdown, and fault behavior affect the physical machine, controller state, and firmware fault handling together.
purpose: Simulate power state, shutdowns, emergency-stop behavior, and realistic fault/halt consequences.
output_state_change: Normal, shutdown, fault, and halt states propagated consistently to firmware responses, telemetry, and logs.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
justification: I mapped Job Model to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it tracks print progress and lifecycle transitions that are shown through build controls and synchronized with firmware job state.
purpose: Simulate believable print progress and job lifecycle effects on the physical printer state.
output_state_change: Progress, elapsed/remaining behavior, active/paused/cancelled state, and synchronized physical activity.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics
justification: I mapped Sensor Model to Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors and Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics because it emulates thermistor, endstop, and filament-sensor behavior and supplies those readings to runtime monitoring.
purpose: Generate sensor behavior from simulated physical state instead of returning fixed or perfect values.
output_state_change: Time-varying sensor readings, limit/endstop state, filament status, and sensor-triggered events.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC)
justification: I mapped Safety Limits to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control and Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC) because safety thresholds are enforced by firmware logic and can trigger controller-level halt, shutdown, or fault actions.
purpose: Apply printer-specific safety thresholds and convert out-of-range actions into believable fault/halt behavior.
output_state_change: Profile-derived limits and consistent warning, fault, shutdown, or halt states propagated across the system.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped System & Access Logs to Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because authentication, API, and session activity are operational events that must be captured through the printer environment's logging path.
purpose: Record authentication attempts, API activity, sessions, and management-surface interactions in a consistent evidence stream.
output_state_change: Timestamped access/session events with actor, endpoint/action, result, and relevant context for later correlation.

am_process_mapping: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network
justification: I mapped G-code & File Artifacts to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network because these artifacts are retained as build-job files and originate from upload or transfer operations into the printer workflow.
purpose: Preserve uploaded or generated G-code/configuration artifacts so attacker-supplied manufacturing content can be reviewed later.
output_state_change: Stored files plus metadata such as filename, size, timestamps, hash, source/session, and execution linkage.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics; Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped Runtime Telemetry to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics, Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors, and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it combines live machine-state analysis, sensor readings, and captured runtime events.
purpose: Capture changing printer state, sensor values, commands, faults, and simulator events while the honeypot is running.
output_state_change: Time-ordered telemetry for motion, extrusion, temperature, power/fault state, print-job state, sensors, and significant events.

am_process_mapping: Stage 5 > Software > MES / PLM feedback systems; Stage 5 > Network > Reporting / API exchange

output_state_change: Analyst-facing views and query results that connect raw evidence to sessions, alerts, artifacts, and state changes.

am_process_mapping: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped Alert Engine to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it evaluates runtime anomalies and faults and then records the resulting alerts as monitored operational events.
purpose: Turn selected suspicious commands, state changes, and fault conditions into analyst-visible alerts.
output_state_change: Structured alerts linked to sessions, commands, artifacts, and relevant printer state.

am_process_mapping: Stage 4 > Software > Traceability / process logging; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
justification: I mapped Session Timeline to Stage 4 > Software > Traceability / process logging and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it reconstructs ordered activity from captured events to provide traceable interaction history.
purpose: Reconstruct the ordered sequence of access, file, command, telemetry, and fault activity across interfaces.
output_state_change: Per-session chronological timelines connecting adversary actions to simulator consequences.

am_process_mapping: Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database
justification: I mapped Evidence Store to Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database because it persistently stores collected HoneyPrint evidence in a database for later querying and analysis.
purpose: Persist captured evidence even when the primary database is unavailable.
output_state_change: Durable structured records in MongoDB or local fallback storage for later analyst queries.

am_process_mapping: Stage 5 > Software > Quality & certification software; Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database
justification: I mapped Artifact Hashing to Stage 5 > Software > Quality & certification software and Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database because SHA-256 provides file-integrity verification and the resulting hash metadata is stored with the evidence records.

output_state_change: Cryptographic hashes stored with artifact metadata and linked to uploads, sessions, and execution records.
